predict.question: Before buying a used car, you can pay eight for an inspection; skipping it nets zero. With it, you choose right 80% of the time and gain ten, otherwise lose ten. What is your expected net payoff after the fee?

exploreHint: Run both cases; compare the changed input.
bookIdea: How to Measure Anything evaluates information by how it can change decisions rather than by precision alone.
modelBoundary: A yields {A}; B {B} over a no-test baseline of zero. Correct decisions gain ten and wrong ones lose ten; increasing the fee subtracts six in both branches. Accuracy and decision payoffs are stipulated; no real measurement’s value is estimated.
doesItHoldUp: Does it hold up? Real-world applicability and the connection to the book remain unverified.
